greek: Καὶ κύριος ἐπεσκέψατο τὴν Σαρραν, καθὰ εἶπεν, καὶ ἐποίησεν κύριος τῇ Σαρρα, καθὰ ἐλάλησεν,
hint: The Lord visits Sarah as he said, and does for her as he spoke.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's ἐπισκέπτομαι is *a pres., which furnishes its tenses to ἐπισκοπέω*: that entry's senses, first *to look upon* or *at, inspect, observe*; *to visit* is its second.
The dative, marked by the article.

greek: καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτεκεν Σαρρα τῷ Αβρααμ υἱὸν εἰς τὸ γῆρας εἰς τὸν καιρόν, καθὰ ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ κύριος.
hint: Sarah conceives and bears Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time God had spoken of.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾĕlōhîm*. The Greek has κύριος.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *lizqūnāyw*, *to his old age*. The Greek has *into the old age*, with no *his*.
One translation, *old age*: plain text, as at 15:15.

names.gloss: (Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Αβρααμ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ τοῦ γενομένου αὐτῷ, ὃν ἔτεκεν αὐτῷ Σαρρα, Ισαακ.
hint: Abraham names the son Sarah bore him Isaac.

notes.text: The repeated article before the participle, plain `the`.

reading: and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of the son of him [[of the one having come into being|of the one having come to be, of the one having arisen, of the one having been brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to him, whom [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] to him [[name:Σαρρα]], [[name:Ισαακ]].

greek: περιέτεμεν δὲ Αβρααμ τὸν Ισαακ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἡμέρᾳ, καθὰ ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ ὁ θεός.
hint: Abraham circumcises Isaac on the eighth day, as God commanded.

notes.text: Stephen has περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ of Isaac, Acts 7:8.
περιτέμνω, the chain of GEN 17:23.

reading: [[cut|cut, clipped round about, pruned, cut off, cut off and hemmed in all round|περιτέμνω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[name:Ισαακ]] to the eighth [[to day|to day, to day-break, to time|ἡμέρα]], [[according as|according as, just as, like as if, exactly as|καθά]] [[enjoined|enjoined, commanded|ἐντέλλομαι]] to him [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]].

greek: Αβρααμ δὲ ἦν ἑκατὸν ἐτῶν, ἡνίκα ἐγένετο αὐτῷ Ισαακ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ.
hint: Abraham is a hundred when Isaac is born.

notes.text: εἰμί of age, the state formula of GEN 1:2 in full, as at 17:24.

reading: [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, hundred of years, [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to him [[name:Ισαακ]] the son of him.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Σαρρα Γέλωτά μοι ἐποίησεν κύριος· ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἀκούσῃ, συγχαρεῖταί μοι.
hint: Sarah: the Lord has made laughter for me; whoever hears will rejoice with me.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾĕlōhîm*. The Greek has κύριος.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *yiṣḥaq-lî*, *will laugh at me* or *with me*, the verb of the name. The Greek has συγχαίρω, *to rejoice with*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐάν.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Σαρρα]] [[laughter|laughter, occasion of laughter and matter for laughter|γέλως]] to me [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]]; who [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] ever [[may hear|may hear, may have hearing of, may hear tell of, may hearken and give ear, may listen to and obey|ἀκούω]], [[will rejoice with|will rejoice with, will take part in joy, will wish joy and congratulate|συγχαίρω]] to me.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Τίς ἀναγγελεῖ τῷ Αβρααμ ὅτι θηλάζει παιδίον Σαρρα; ὅτι ἔτεκον υἱὸν ἐν τῷ γήρει μου.
hint: Who would have told Abraham that Sarah nurses a child? For I bore a son in my old age.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *hênîqâ bānîm*, *nursed sons*. The Greek has the singular, *a young child*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *lizqūnāyw*, *in his old age*. The Greek has *in my old age*.
θηλάζω is first, of the mother, *to suckle*; of the young, *to suck*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] who [[will carry back tidings of|will carry back tidings of, will report|ἀναγγέλλω]] to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[suckles|suckles, sucks|θηλάζω]] [[young child|young child, a slave-lad|παιδίον]] [[name:Σαρρα]]? [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[I brought into the world|I brought into the world, I brought forth, I bore, I produced|τίκτω]] a son in the old age of me.

greek: Καὶ ηὐξήθη τὸ παιδίον καὶ ἀπεγαλακτίσθη, καὶ ἐποίησεν Αβρααμ δοχὴν μεγάλην, ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ἀπεγαλακτίσθη Ισαακ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ.
hint: The child grows and is weaned, and Abraham makes a great feast the day Isaac is weaned.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ's ἀπογαλακτίζω, one translation, *wean from the mother's milk*: plain text, in the passive.
δοχή is first *a receptacle*; *a reception, entertainment* is its second.
αὐξάνω in the passive, the chain of GEN 8:17.

reading: And [[was made large|was made large, was increased and augmented, was increased in power and strengthened and exalted, was promoted to honour and glorified and magnified, grew and waxed and increased, grew up|αὐξάνω]] [[the young child|the young child, the slave-lad|παιδίον]] and was weaned from the mother's milk, and [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[a receptacle|a receptacle, a reception and entertainment|δοχή]] [[big|big, great, tall, full-grown, vast and high, spacious and wide, strong and mighty, violent, loud, prevailing, weighty and important|μέγας]], to which [[to day|to day, to day-break, to time|ἡμέρα]] was weaned from the mother's milk [[name:Ισαακ]] the son of him.

greek: ἰδοῦσα δὲ Σαρρα τὸν υἱὸν Αγαρ τῆς Αἰγυπτίας, ὃς ἐγένετο τῷ Αβρααμ, παίζοντα μετὰ Ισαακ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτῆς
hint: Sarah sees Hagar's son playing with her son Isaac.

notes.lemma: παίζοντα μετὰ Ισαακ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτῆς
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *mĕṣaḥēq*, *laughing* or *playing*, with nothing after it. The Greek adds *with Isaac her son*. Paul reads the scene at Galatians 4:29, ὁ κατὰ σάρκα γεννηθεὶς ἐδίωκε τὸν κατὰ πνεῦμα.
παίζω is first *to play like a child, to sport, play*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἑαυτῆς.
Rahlfs prints no punctuation at the end of the verse.

names.gloss: (Αγαρ, from Hebrew Hāgār, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ εἶπεν τῷ Αβρααμ Ἔκβαλε τὴν παιδίσκην ταύτην καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς· οὐ γὰρ κληρονομήσει ὁ υἱὸς τῆς παιδίσκης ταύτης μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ μου Ισαακ.
hint: Cast out this slave woman and her son; he shall not inherit with my son Isaac.

notes.lemma: Ἔκβαλε … μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ μου Ισαακ
notes.text: Paul quotes the verse at Galatians 4:30, Ἔκβαλε τὴν παιδίσκην καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς, οὐ γὰρ μὴ κληρονομήσει ὁ υἱὸς τῆς παιδίσκης μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἐλευθέρας, without ταύτην and with *of the free woman* for *my son Isaac*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds μή after οὐ γάρ and leaves out the second ταύτης, as Paul's quotation reads.
κληρονομέω, the chain of GEN 15:3.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[throw|throw, cast out of, throw out, cast out and banish, depose, throw away and reject|ἐκβάλλω]] [[the young girl|the young girl, the maiden, the young slave, the courtesan|παιδίσκη]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] and the son of her; not [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] [[will receive a share of an inheritance|will receive a share of an inheritance and inherit a portion, will inherit, will be an inheritor, will succeed|κληρονομέω]] the son [[of the young girl|of the young girl, of the maiden, of the young slave, of the courtesan|παιδίσκη]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of the son of me of [[name:Ισαακ]].

greek: σκληρὸν δὲ ἐφάνη τὸ ῥῆμα σφόδρα ἐναντίον Αβρααμ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ.
hint: The word is very hard in Abraham's eyes because of his son.

notes.text: φαίνω in the passive: the active's *to bring to light, make to appear* first, and the passive's own *to come to light, be seen, appear* last.

[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds Ισμαηλ at the end.

hint: God: let it not be hard; listen to Sarah, for in Isaac seed shall be called for you.

παιδίον, the chain of GEN 17:12.

hint: The slave woman's son too I will make a great nation, for he is your seed.

greek: ἀνέστη δὲ Αβρααμ τὸ πρωὶ καὶ ἔλαβεν ἄρτους καὶ ἀσκὸν ὕδατος καὶ ἔδωκεν Αγαρ καὶ ἐπέθηκεν ἐπὶ τὸν ὦμον καὶ τὸ παιδίον καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτήν. ἀπελθοῦσα δὲ ἐπλανᾶτο τὴν ἔρημον κατὰ τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ ὅρκου.
hint: Abraham gives Hagar bread and a skin of water on her shoulder, with the child, and sends her away; she wanders in the desert by the well of the oath.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾēr šābaʿ*, the name Beersheba. The Greek has *the well of the oath*, the name translated.

greek: ἐξέλιπεν δὲ τὸ ὕδωρ ἐκ τοῦ ἀσκοῦ, καὶ ἔρριψεν τὸ παιδίον ὑποκάτω μιᾶς ἐλάτης·

greek: ἀπελθοῦσα δὲ ἐκάθητο ἀπέναντι αὐτοῦ μακρόθεν ὡσεὶ τόξου βολήν· εἶπεν γάρ Οὐ μὴ ἴδω τὸν θάνατον τοῦ παιδίου μου. καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἀπέναντι αὐτοῦ, ἀναβοῆσαν δὲ τὸ παιδίον ἔκλαυσεν.
hint: She sits a bowshot away: I will not see the child die. The child cries out and weeps.

greek: καὶ ἀνέῳξεν ὁ θεὸς τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς, καὶ εἶδεν φρέαρ ὕδατος ζῶντος καὶ ἐπορεύθη καὶ ἔπλησεν τὸν ἀσκὸν ὕδατος καὶ ἐπότισεν τὸ παιδίον.
hint: God opens her eyes; she sees a well of living water, fills the skin and gives the child a drink.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾēr māyim*, *a well of water*. The Greek adds *living*.

greek: καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετὰ τοῦ παιδίου, καὶ ηὐξήθη. καὶ κατῴκησεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ἐγένετο δὲ τοξότης.

Middle Liddell is first *a bowman, archer*.

hint: He lives in the desert of Paran, and his mother takes him a wife from Egypt.

hint: Abimelech, with Ahuzzath his bride's escort and Phicol his army chief, says to Abraham: God is with you in all you do.

greek: νῦν οὖν ὄμοσόν μοι τὸν θεὸν μὴ ἀδικήσειν με μηδὲ τὸ σπέρμα μου μηδὲ τὸ ὄνομά μου, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ἣν ἐποίησα μετὰ σοῦ, ποιήσεις μετʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ τῇ γῇ, ᾗ σὺ παρῴκησας ἐν αὐτῇ.

The future infinitive of ἀδικέω, whose first sense is *to do wrong*; the active's senses, as the passive took them at 16:5.

ὁρκισμός, one translation, *administration of an oath*: plain text.

names.gloss: (Φρέαρ, "a well", the first word of the name the verse gives the place, for Hebrew Bĕʾēr šebaʿ)

greek: καὶ διέθεντο διαθήκην ἐν τῷ φρέατι τοῦ ὅρκου. ἀνέστη δὲ Αβιμελεχ καὶ Οχοζαθ ὁ νυμφαγωγὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ Φικολ ὁ ἀρχιστράτηγος τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν γῆν τῶν Φυλιστιιμ.
hint: They make a covenant at the well of the oath; Abimelech, Ahuzzath and Phicol return to the land of the Philistines.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew of this verse, as at 21:22.
The article before a people's name is not printed, as at 10:16.
ἐπιστρέφω, the chain of GEN 8:12.

reading: and [[arranged as they liked|arranged as they liked, disposed of, disposed of their property and devised it by will, set out for sale and disposed of, arranged mutually, made a covenant with, settled with|διατίθεμαι]] [[a disposition|a disposition of property by will, a will and testament, an arrangement between two parties, a covenant|διαθήκη]] [[in the well|within, inside of, and by means of the well, the tank and cistern and reservoir, the oil jar|ἐν; φρέαρ]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath|ὅρκος]]. [[stood up|stood up, rose, rose to fight against, rose to go and set out|ἀνίστημι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Αβιμελεχ]] and [[name:Οχοζαθ]] the leader of the bride of him and [[name:Φικολ]] the commander-in-chief [[of the power|of the power, of the might, of the strength, of the ability, of the authority, of the force for war and forces, of the quantity, of the faculty and capacity, of the force and meaning, of the worth and value|δύναμις]] of him and [[turned about|turned about, turned round, returned, turned towards, corrected and made to repent|ἐπιστρέφω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] of [[name:Φυλιστιιμ]].

names.gloss: (Φυλιστιιμ, from Hebrew Pĕlištîm, the people of Pĕlešet)

greek: καὶ ἐφύτευσεν Αβρααμ ἄρουραν ἐπὶ τῷ φρέατι τοῦ ὅρκου καὶ ἐπεκαλέσατο ἐκεῖ τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου Θεὸς αἰώνιος.
hint: Abraham plants a plot by the well of the oath and calls there on the name of the Lord, Everlasting God.

notes.lemma: ἄρουραν ἐπὶ τῷ φρέατι τοῦ ὅρκου
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾēšel bibʾēr šābaʿ*, *a tamarisk in Beersheba*. The Greek has ἄρουρα, *tilled land*, *at the well of the oath*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾēl ʿôlām*. The Greek has θεός, anarthrous, capitalised by Rahlfs as the name called on.
Middle Liddell is first *tilled* or *arable land*.
Capitalised because it is the name called upon, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[planted|planted, planted for himself, begot, produced and brought about and caused|φυτεύω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[tilled land|tilled land, arable land, seed-land, cornland, land and earth, a woman as bearing children, a measure of land|ἄρουρα]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] [[to the well|to the well, to the tank and cistern and reservoir, to the oil jar|φρέαρ]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath|ὅρκος]] and [[called upon|called upon, invoked and appealed to, invited, called in as a helper, was called by surname|ἐπικαλέω]] [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting, eternal|αἰώνιος]].

greek: παρῴκησεν δὲ Αβρααμ ἐν τῇ γῇ τῶν Φυλιστιιμ ἡμέρας πολλάς.
hint: Abraham sojourns many days in the land of the Philistines.

notes.text: The accusative of extent, ἡμέρα and πολύς.

reading: [[dwelt beside|dwelt beside, dwelt along the coast of, lived near, dwelt among, lay near, lived in and sojourned|παροικέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the earth, the land, the ground|ἐν; γῆ]] of [[name:Φυλιστιιμ]] [[days|days, day-breaks, times|ἡμέρα]] [[many|many, often, much and mighty and great, deep, loud, strong, large and wide, far, long|πολύς]].
